results.title: Strengthened Benders Cuts for Stochastic Integer Programs with Continuous Recourse | Request PDF
results.content: [4] investigate the strength of integrality-based cuts in conjunction with Benders cuts for stochastic integer programs with continuous recourse, and use test instances of the SNIP problem to demonstrate the value of integrality-based cuts within Benders decomposition. In this paper, we propose a novel decomposition approach for mixed-integer stochastic programming (SMIP) problems that is inspired by the combination of penalty-based Lagrangian and block Gauss-Seidel methods (PBGS). In this article, we discuss ways to use these cuts within the framework of Benders’ decomposition algorithms for solving two-stage mixed-binary stochastic problems with binary first-stage variables and continuous recourse. We utilize scenario-based CMIR cuts for TSS-CMIPs and their distributionally robust generalizations with structured CMIPs in the second stage, and prove that these cuts provide conic/linear programming equivalent or approximation for the second stage CMIPs. We also perform extensive computational experiments by solving stochastic and distributionally robust capacitated facility location problem and randomly generated structured TSS-CMIPs with polyhedral CMIPs and second-order CMIPs in the second stage, i.e. p=1 and p=2, respectively. Computational results demonstrate that our proposed method improves the Benders relaxation significantly faster than previous methods for generating Lagrangian cuts and, when used within a branch-and-cut algorithm, significantly reduces the size of the search tree for two classes of test problems. Computational results demonstrate that our proposed method improves the Benders relaxation significantly faster than previous methods for generating Lagrangian cuts and, when used within a branch-and-cut algorithm, significantly reduces the size of the search tree for three classes of test problems. Stochastic-programming models are computationally challenging for large-scale problem instances, and, therefore, we propose a solution technique based on Benders cuts. Our heuristic algorithm demonstrates a significantly improved capacity to handle large-size two-stage problems comparing to three conventional methods for stochastic integer programming, and solving the two-stage model by our heuristic in a rolling horizon provides a good approximation of the multistage problem. This paper presents a first computational study of a disjunctive cutting plane method for stochastic mixed 0-1 programs that uses lift-and-project cuts based on the extensive form of the two-stage SMIP problem. We present an algorithm for solving stochastic integer programming problems with recourse, based on a dual decomposition scheme and Lagrangian relaxation.

results.title: Advanced Integer Programming Techniques
results.content: Integer programming is a powerful tool for modeling and solving complex optimization problems in various fields, including logistics, finance, and energy management. This article explores advanced integer programming techniques, focusing on decomposition methods, heuristic approaches, and the integration of integer programming with other optimization techniques. Decomposition techniques are essential for tackling large-scale integer programming problems by breaking them down into more manageable subproblems. Benders' decomposition is a widely used technique for solving mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) problems. The master problem contains the integer variables, while the subproblem is a linear program that is solved for a given set of integer variables. Heuristic and metaheuristic methods are used to find good-quality solutions to integer programming problems within a reasonable computational time.
